sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Another Counsel for Applicant :- Vijay Prakash Mishra
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.

Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the material available on record.

This application for anticipatory bail has been filed by applicant - Nishant Kumar Sharma in connection with Case Crime No.0086 of 2022, under Sections 420, 467, 468 & 471 I.P.C., P.S.-
Ahmadgarh, District- Bulandshahar.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is innocent and has no concern with the present matter.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false.
Investigation is going on in the matter.
Applicant's case is squarely covered under Section 438 Cr.P.C.
If the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty and will cooperate with the investigation.
The applicant has apprehension of his arrest by the police any time.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.

It is alleged against the applicant that one complaint was made by him against the named accused namely, Brijesh, Aman and 3-4 unknown persons, under Sections 354, 452, 506, 379 I.P.C., 7/8 Nishant Kumar Sharma vs State Of U.P. And Another on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97868246/
1 POCSO Act and 67 of the Information Technology Act, 2008, P.S.- Arnia, District- Bulandshahar.
Subsequently, it was found that date-of-birth certificate regarding the victim of that case namely,
Km. Sarvesh which was provided by the present applicant was forged then this F.I.R. was lodged against Shri Kuldeep Sharma, Principal of Kisan Higher Secondary School, Domla, Hasangarh,
District- Bulandshahar.

entities.text: Nishant Kumar Sharma vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The present accused-applicant is not named in the F.I.R..

It also appears from the perusal of the record that Shri Kuldeep Sharma, the co-accused of this matter has already been granted anticipatory bail by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 30.6.2022 passed in CRIMINAL MISC ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION U/S 438 CR.P.C. No. - 5646 of 2022 (Kuldeep Sharma Vs. State of U.P.).

entities.text: Kuldeep Sharma Vs. State of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1, it has been held that while considering an application for grant of anticipatory bail, the court has to consider the nature of the offence, the role of the person, the likelihood of his influencing the course of investigation, or tampering with evidence including intimidating witnesses, llikelihood of fleeing justice, such as leaving the country, etc.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has further been held that Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case, while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail, or refuse it.
Whether to grant or not is a matter of discretion.

Considering the settled principles of law regarding anticipatory bail, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion of the merits of the case, in my view, it is a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant till submission of report under Section 173(2)
Cr.P.C. in the matter.
The anticipatory bail application is allowed.

In the event of arrest of the applicant in the aforesaid case crime, he shall be released on anticipatory bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions :-
1.
The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required.

2. The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
3.
The applicant shall not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
4. The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.
